label: Born in Breslau
description: Fritz Haber was born into a Jewish family in Breslau.

sources.quote: Fritz Haber (1868–1934) ... earned the name of Germany's "Doctor Death".

label: First ammonia synthesis
description: First millilitres of ammonia from atmospheric nitrogen flowed from laboratory apparatus.

sources.quote: In July 1909, the first millilitres of ammonia containing exclusively atmospheric nitrogen, unavailable before, flowed from their tabletop laboratory apparatus.

label: Directed chlorine gas attack at Ypres
description: Haber personally directed the first successful chlorine gas attack on French and English lines.

sources.quote: Less than a year later, on 22 April 1915, Haber personally directed the German chlorine gas attack at Ypres.

label: Clara Immerwahr committed suicide
description: Haber's wife committed suicide in protest at his work on chemical weapons.

sources.quote: The marriage had its epilogue on 1 May 1915 at Dahlem
committed suicide in protest at his work

label: Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry
description: Awarded the Nobel Prize for developing a method for the direct synthesis of ammonia.

sources.quote: He was awarded the Nobel Prize in chemistry in 1919 for developing a method for the direct synthesis of ammonia from its elements: hydrogen and nitrogen .

label: Gold from seawater project
description: Haber pursued a project to extract gold from sea water to help Germany pay reparations.

sources.quote: Haber's project to extract gold from sea water, pursued from 1920 to 1926, and involving several ocean voyages, ended in failure

label: Left Germany for exile
description: Haber left Germany after Hitler's rise to power and went into exile in England.

sources.quote: In one of his last letters, Haber, already in exile in England, wrote the following to Bosch: ... 28 December 1933

label: Died in Basel
description: Haber died in Basel a year after leaving Germany.

sources.quote: A year later, having left Germany, he died in Basel.
